title: Phenotype of Alcohol-Related Nutritional Sensory Neuronopathies and Comparison With Dysimmune and Paraneoplastic Forms
official: Phenotype of Alcohol-Related Nutritional Sensory Neuronopathies and Comparison With Dysimmune and Paraneoplastic Forms
summary: Sensory neuronopathies (SNNs) are rare disorders characterized by damage to sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia. They may have dysimmune, paraneoplastic, toxic, or genetic causes. Alcohol-related nutritional sensory neuronopathy has recently been described and may present acutely or subacutely with pain, mimicking dysimmune or paraneoplastic disease. Distinguishing these causes early may help guide appropriate management. This international, multicentre, retrospective observational cohort study will describe the initial and follow-up clinical and electrophysiological phenotype of acute/subacute alcohol-related nutritional SNN and compare it with dysimmune and paraneoplastic SNN. Data will be abstracted from existing medical records. The protocol anticipates approximately 75 participants with alcohol-related nutritional SNN, 50 with dysimmune SNN, and 20 with paraneoplastic SNN. No additional procedure is performed for research purposes and no direct benefit is expected for participants.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria :

* Age ≥ 18 years.
* Probable sensory neuronopathy according to the diagnostic criteria of Camdessanché et al.
* Acute or subacute onset (0-6 months).
* One of the following aetiologies: Alcohol-related nutritional SNN: chronic alcohol misuse (\>100 g/week for at least 3 months) and/or biological markers of alcohol consumption, with dysimmune and paraneoplastic causes excluded. The minimum work-up includes an immune laboratory assessment including serum anti-neuronal antibodies, lumbar puncture, and thoraco-abdominal imaging. Dysimmune SNN: associated with Sjögren's syndrome, lupus, primary biliary cholangitis, anti-FGFR3 antibodies, or anti-AGO antibodies. Paraneoplastic SNN: associated with anti-Hu or anti-CV2/CRMP5 antibodies.

Exclusion Criteria :

* Exposure to platinum salts before the onset of sensory neuronopathy.
* Known hereditary neuropathy.
* Patient under guardianship or curatorship (tutelle or curatelle).
* Patient objection to the use of their data for the study.
